quarterly_data.signal: Multi-year CapEx profile quantified beyond the earnings call: 'If you look at just our CapEx profile, we have gone from just over $13 billion of CapEx in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026, we'll do double of that. Then we have pointed to Fiscal 2027 being above $45 billion even.' Sadana adds that the U.S. commitment has been taken from $200 billion up to $250 billion and the timeline for when that $250 billion is invested has been PULLED IN.

quarterly_data.signal: Fab-by-fab buildout schedule: Micron has 20 investment projects going on around the world of all different shapes and sizes, bringing on both front-end and back-end capacity. Idaho ID1 has first wafer outs in mid next year; ID2 follows right after with first wafer outs close to the end of calendar 2028. The Tongluo fab purchased in Taiwan has wafer starts in 2027 with further expansions there, plus expansions in Japan and Singapore. In New York Micron has a four-fab cluster with first fab output expected in 2030 - it broke ground in January and has hit the concrete pour milestone ahead of schedule - alongside the Manassas fab in Virginia. Management flags construction talent as a genuine bottleneck: there are not enough skilled construction workers or fab technicians given simultaneous data center, power plant and semiconductor buildouts.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 investment projects worldwide; Idaho ID1 first wafer outs mid next year, ID2 close to the end of calendar 2028; Tongluo wafer starts in 2027; New York four-fab cluster first output 2030

quarterly_data.signal: When industry supply actually arrives: 'We think that meaningful supply will start to ramp only in 2028. And that too, it'll be only an initial ramp. It'll gather momentum only in the years after. It will take a while for the industry to find a new equilibrium point. But when exactly that happens, we don't have line of sight to yet.' Because tech transitions no longer produce enough bit growth, the whole industry needs greenfield clean room space at the same time, which is gated by construction, permitting and infrastructure. Cycle-time context on why memory supply cannot respond quickly: roughly 2,000 process steps in the fab, three and a half plus months (approaching four months) through the fab plus a month - or a month and a half for more complex products - in assembly, packaging and test, so about a five-month cycle time from wafer start to customer shipment.
quarterly_data.figure: meaningful industry supply ramps only in 2028 (initial ramp); ~2,000 process steps and a five-month cycle time from wafer start to shipment

quarterly_data.signal: Memory content per humanoid robot quantified as the next demand wave after data center and edge: 'Each humanoid is going to have hundreds of gigabytes of DRAM content and terabytes of SSD NAND content. They are going to be massive drivers of growth in demand for both DRAM and NAND.' Management expects robotics to start in factory-automation settings and become a massive growth driver in the latter part of this decade and into the 2030s, a wave that compounds on top of data center demand rather than replacing it.
quarterly_data.figure: hundreds of gigabytes of DRAM content and terabytes of SSD NAND content per humanoid
